strand_a.summary: Geoeconomic Exposure and EU Industrial Policy: Export Dependence Amid US–China Techno‐Nationalist Rivalry. strand_a.summary: In recent years, the European Union (EU) has faced mounting challenges in promoting and safeguarding democracy in its neighbourhood, as autocratisation trends, entangled with intensifying geopolitical competition, have progressively reshaped the conditions under which EU democracy-support instruments operate. dynamic_shocks.title: An export restriction abruptly cuts Europe's access to semiconductor supply and production
dynamic_shocks.plainly: Europe relies on semiconductor supply and production. Separate primary evidence shows that an external export restriction can change access quickly. Recent weak signals and historical material may strengthen the context, but neither can establish the shock on its own.
dynamic_shocks.second_order: Projects may keep their grants and institutions but still lose time, access or usable capacity while a replacement is found.
dynamic_shocks.why_easy_to_miss: The hypothesis appears when durable European capability evidence and a separately evidenced external pressure are read as one chain; low-weight current signals and history are then used only as context.
reasoning: Primary retained evidence shows European reliance on or expansion of semiconductor supply and production.
Separate primary retained evidence shows a live mechanism for an external export restriction.
Primary evidence contains 2 direct capability × pressure coupling record(s).
2 recent weak-signal item(s) point in the same direction; each is capped at 30% of a primary evidence item and none satisfies a primary threshold.
2 historical Strand-A item(s) provide structural context; they cannot serve as the current trigger.
The scenario becomes a shock only if the response is slower than the disruption.
conditions: Europe materially depends on semiconductor supply and production for current or planned work.
An external export restriction reaches the supplier, service, partner or rule that the European capability depends on.
Europe cannot substitute, reroute or absorb the change before projects begin losing usable capacity.
case_against: The primary corpus contains 1 strong sign(s) of substitution, resilience or policy response that could absorb the shock.
Recent media/weak-signal corroboration is intentionally down-weighted and cannot substitute for primary evidence.
The scenario still depends on the disruption arriving faster than Europe can respond.
prevention_actions: Qualify alternative suppliers for legacy and advanced chips before a disruption.
Expand European production where dependence is most concentrated.
Secure alternative suppliers and stocks before a new export rule takes effect.
watch_for: A supplier country expands export licensing to an input Europe relies on.
European firms report delayed or denied licences.
dynamic_shocks.net_assessment: Well supported enough to watch closely, with contextual signals reinforcing rather than carrying the case.

support.core_message: The cases cover both implemented measures and threats, ranging from trade and investment restrictions to export controls, procurement discrimination, extraterritorial sanctions, supply curtailments and other forms of economic pressure. dynamic_shocks.title: A partner weaponises Europe's dependence on critical technologies and know-how to extract concessions
dynamic_shocks.plainly: Europe relies on critical technologies and know-how. Separate primary evidence shows that economic coercion can change access quickly. Recent weak signals and historical material may strengthen the context, but neither can establish the shock on its own.
dynamic_shocks.second_order: Projects may keep their grants and institutions but still lose time, access or usable capacity while a replacement is found.
dynamic_shocks.why_easy_to_miss: The hypothesis appears when durable European capability evidence and a separately evidenced external pressure are read as one chain; low-weight current signals and history are then used only as context.
reasoning: Primary retained evidence shows European reliance on or expansion of critical technologies and know-how.
Separate primary retained evidence shows a live mechanism for economic coercion.
Primary evidence contains 1 direct capability × pressure coupling record(s).
2 historical Strand-A item(s) provide structural context; they cannot serve as the current trigger.
The scenario becomes a shock only if the response is slower than the disruption.
conditions: Europe materially depends on critical technologies and know-how for current or planned work.
Economic coercion reaches the supplier, service, partner or rule that the European capability depends on.
Europe cannot substitute, reroute or absorb the change before projects begin losing usable capacity.
case_against: Only one primary retained record currently links the European capability directly to the outside pressure.
The primary direct connection is concentrated in one source, so independent confirmation is still weak.
The primary corpus contains 5 strong sign(s) of substitution, resilience or policy response that could absorb the shock.
The scenario still depends on the disruption arriving faster than Europe can respond.
prevention_actions: Coordinate export controls and screening with partners to avoid leakage around the edges.
Keep safeguards targeted so ordinary openness survives.
Make the anti-coercion response credible and fast, and coordinate it with partners.

The Commission opens an anti-coercion examination.

objects.reason: Current cleaned evidence no longer satisfies the repository's current construction threshold for this downstream object.

previous_object.title: A trading partner's sudden tariffs undercut Europe's Europe's industrial base
previous_object.plainly: Europe relies on Europe's industrial base. Separate primary evidence shows that a partner's tariff escalation can change access quickly. Recent weak signals and historical material may strengthen the context, but neither can establish the shock on its own.
previous_object.second_order: Projects may keep their grants and institutions but still lose time, access or usable capacity while a replacement is found.
previous_object.why_easy_to_miss: The hypothesis appears when durable European capability evidence and a separately evidenced external pressure are read as one chain; low-weight current signals and history are then used only as context.
reasoning: Primary retained evidence shows European reliance on or expansion of Europe's industrial base.
Separate primary retained evidence shows a live mechanism for a partner's tariff escalation.
Primary evidence contains 5 direct capability × pressure coupling record(s).
2 recent weak-signal item(s) point in the same direction; each is capped at 30% of a primary evidence item and none satisfies a primary threshold.
2 historical Strand-A item(s) provide structural context; they cannot serve as the current trigger.
The scenario becomes a shock only if the response is slower than the disruption.
conditions: Europe materially depends on Europe's industrial base for current or planned work.
A partner's tariff escalation reaches the supplier, service, partner or rule that the European capability depends on.
Europe cannot substitute, reroute or absorb the change before projects begin losing usable capacity.
case_against: The primary corpus contains 5 strong sign(s) of substitution, resilience or policy response that could absorb the shock.
Recent media/weak-signal corroboration is intentionally down-weighted and cannot substitute for primary evidence.
The scenario still depends on the disruption arriving faster than Europe can respond.
prevention_actions: Use trade-defence tools quickly against distorted competition.
Lower structural costs such as energy so protection is not the only answer.
Keep credible, proportionate countermeasures and market alternatives ready.
watch_for: A partner announces new tariffs on European goods.
Europe prepares countermeasures.
previous_object.net_assessment: Plausible, but important parts of the primary trigger or connection still need confirmation.
